# Modules Repo Workflow

An org can link ONE git repository to its control plane as the canonical home of
its custom IaC modules. When that link exists, **module development happens in
that repo** — clone → branch → author → PR — and CI owns publishing. Direct
`raptor publish` is only the escape hatch. This skill is the shared preamble for
`/build-facets-module`.

## Step 0 — Detect (always, per control plane)

```bash
raptor get modules-repo -o json
```

- **Error / "no modules repo"** → not linked. Use the classic direct-upload flow
  from the calling skill, and see [Not linked?](#not-linked) below for a one-time
  nudge. Stop reading here.
- **Linked** → the JSON carries `gitUrl`, `defaultBranch`, `pathPrefix`,
  `enforcementMode`, `ciUserName`. Tell the user up front:
  *"Your org's modules live in `<gitUrl>` — I'll develop there and publish via PR."*

Detection is per control plane: if a task touches several profiles (e.g. a sandbox
CP for QA and a prod CP), run it against each — a sandbox CP is typically NOT
linked even when prod is.

The CP registration is the only source of truth. Never guess the repo from memory,
org convention, or an existing local clone.

## The repo-first workflow (linked orgs)

**1. Get a checkout and branch.**

```bash
git clone <gitUrl> && cd <repo>          # or reuse an existing clone
git checkout <defaultBranch> && git pull  # always branch from fresh default
git checkout -b <feature-branch>
```

**2. Author at the canonical path.**

Modules live at `{pathPrefix}/modules/{intent}/{flavor}/{version}/` (no
`{pathPrefix}/` segment when pathPrefix is empty). Scaffold with
`raptor module init` directly at that path, or edit the existing version dir.

- **Never** author in scratch dirs or forks of other module repos when linked.
- **Never** edit a CP-downloaded copy (`raptor module download`,
  `get iac-module --save-to`) and re-upload it — those are read-only inspection
  tools; editing them orphans the git history and fails ENFORCE.

**3. Inner loop — iterate with PREVIEW uploads (unchanged, fast).**

```bash
raptor create iac-module -f <module-dir> --auto-create   # PREVIEW upload
```

Run it from inside the branch checkout: provenance (remote URL + commit SHA) is
recorded automatically. Previews are never blocked by enforcement, so test in a
test project as usual. Commit before uploading if you want the recorded SHA to
match what you'll push.

**4. Publish = PR, not `raptor publish`.**

```bash
git add -A && git commit -m "<change>"
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
gh pr create --title "<change>" --body "<what/why>"
gh pr checks --watch        # CI: terraform validate, trivy, dry-run, preview upload
```

On the PR, CI registers a feature-branch preview and comments on the PR. **On
merge, CI re-uploads at the merge SHA and publishes** — nothing else to do.
Report the PR URL and check status to the user; publishing lands when the PR does.

**5. The escape hatch (`raptor publish iac-module`).**

Keep it for emergencies only, and warn the user by enforcement mode:

| Mode | What direct publish does |
|---|---|
| `OFF` | Works silently. Still bypasses review/CI — say so. |
| `WARN` | Works, but raptor prints a provenance warning when the upload didn't come from a clean clone of the linked repo. Treat the warning as a bug in the flow, not noise. |
| `ENFORCE` | Rejected unless the upload recorded a commit SHA and its git URL matches the linked repo — i.e. it only works from a clone of that repo. |

## CI / preview lifecycle facts (do not fight these)

- **Single preview slot per module group** (intent/flavor/version). Concurrent
  PRs touching the same module: last write wins; the CI comment tells you whose
  preview currently occupies the slot.
- Merge CI does **not** promote the PR's preview — it re-uploads at the merge SHA
  and publishes that.
- Preview cleanup happens only on PR **close-without-merge**, and only via
  `raptor delete iac-module REF --stage PREVIEW`. Plain delete-by-ref resolves
  the PUBLISHED doc when both exist — never use it for cleanup.
- Headless/CI raptor auth is the env triplet `CONTROL_PLANE_URL`,
  `FACETS_USERNAME`, `FACETS_TOKEN` (`raptor login` is interactive-only).
- Publish-on-merge automation is GitHub-only today. For GitLab/Bitbucket-linked
  repos: author in the repo and merge a PR/MR all the same, then run the escape
  hatch from an up-to-date clone of the default branch so provenance matches.

## Not linked?

Continue with the calling skill's direct-upload flow. Once per conversation (not
more), mention the golden path:

> Your org has no modules repo linked. A linked repo gives modules git history,
> PR review, CI validation, and publish provenance. Set one up with
> `raptor module bootstrap-repo` (GitHub accounts; migrates existing published
> modules) or the Module Registry page → *Connect a modules repo*.

If the user wants it, `raptor module bootstrap-repo --help` covers the flags
(`--repo-url` XOR `--create-repo`, `--vcs-account`, `--path-prefix`, …).

## Getting the repo on disk (surface-specific)

Locally, plain `git clone`/`git push` and `gh pr create` under the user's own
credentials are exactly right. Prefer SSH remotes if the user's other clones
use SSH.
